key_points.point: Altman argues that the energy consumption of AI is justified by its potential to solve complex global challenges, framing the energy cost of AI as comparable to the energy cost of human development.
key_points.verbatim: “People talk about how much energy it takes to train an AI model – but it also takes a lot of energy to train a human,” Altman told the Indian Express recently while in India for the AI Impact summit.

key_points.point: Altman advocates for a rapid transition to sustainable energy sources like nuclear, wind, and solar to power the infrastructure required for AI development.
key_points.verbatim: “We need to move towards nuclear or wind and solar very quickly.”

key_points.point: Altman dismisses concerns about water usage in modern datacenters as outdated, asserting that newer infrastructure has moved away from water-intensive cooling methods.
key_points.verbatim: “Water is totally fake. It used to be true. We used to do evaporative cooling in datacenters, but now … we don’t do that,” Altman said.

key_points.point: Environmental groups argue that the rapid, unregulated expansion of datacenters for AI threatens community resources and climate security, calling for a moratorium on new construction.
key_points.verbatim: “The rapid, largely unregulated rise of datacenters to fuel the AI and crypto frenzy is disrupting communities across the country and threatening Americans’ economic, environmental, climate and water security,” their letter states.

key_points.point: Experts highlight that the current pace of datacenter construction forces reliance on fossil fuel-based power, undermining sustainability goals.
key_points.verbatim: “The pace at which companies are building new datacenters means the bulk of the electricity to power them must come from fossil fuel-based power plants.”

key_points.point: Critics question the justification for AI's massive energy consumption, noting that the majority of AI usage is not directed toward solving critical global problems.
key_points.verbatim: A September 2025 report from OpenAI on how people use ChatGPT found that 70% of messages to the bot were not work related.

key_points.point: Critics argue that Altman’s comparison between human development and AI training is dehumanizing and morally bankrupt, distracting from the environmental destruction caused by AI infrastructure.
key_points.verbatim: “He’s saying a really big spreadsheet and a baby are morally equivalent,” Matt Stoller, research director at the American Economic Liberties Project, posted on X. “One reason to believe that life is divine is so that you don’t allow sociopaths like this anywhere near anything important.”

factual_claims.claim: Datacenters accounted for 1.5% of global electricity consumption in 2024 and are projected to grow by 15% annually through 2030.
OpenAI research indicates that 70% of ChatGPT messages are not work-related.
